The D-HGNRs have **two CD peaks, at 585 nm and 790 nm** (page 3). The paper says both the L- and D-HGNRs show "mirror-image chiral responses with two distinct chiroptical peaks at 585 nm and 790 nm" (Fig. 1c).

From the plot in Fig. 1c (page 4), the D-HGNRs have a positive peak near 585 nm (about +370 mdeg) and a negative peak near 790 nm (about −250 mdeg). The L-HGNRs show the opposite signs. These signs and amplitudes are my reading of the figure; the text gives only the wavelengths.

The text also gives g-factors of −0.0151 and 0.0150 "respectively" (page 3). It's unclear whether "respectively" refers to the two peaks or to the L and D forms.
